full_judgment:
9. The contention raised by Mr. Hyder Ali that the order of review was passed coram non judice because of the intrusion of the Sessions Judge in the review process also could not be accepted. Because we could not find anything in the record revealing that the CMLA sat with anyone else in passing the order of review. We could not find any defect or deviation in the formation of the review body. 

 On a reference to Regulation No. 3(4) which is as under: "The Chief Martial Law Administrator or, as the case may be, Zonal Martial Law Administrator may, on review, confirm, set aside, (enhance) vary or modify any order, judgment or sentence or make orders for retrial or such other orders as he deems necessary for the ends of Justice," we find that the reviewing authority has to exercise his power of review for the ends of justice". We also find that in the Martial Law dispensation of justice there is no appeal or revision against the judgment and order of the trial Court. There is a review from the judgment of the Martial Law Court and that is final. In view of the expression "for the ends of justice "and the finality of the order after review particularly when an order of acquittal is under review, we are of opinion that the reviewing authority cannot exercise the power of review in a casual, mechanical or capricious manner and instead he has to do it by proper application of judicial mind.
